```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lessR)
library(readxl)
library(BSDA)
read_excel("~/Downloads/butterflies_pesticides.xlsx")
butterflies_pesticide <-read_excel("~/Downloads/butterflies_pesticides.xlsx")
bp <- butterflies_pesticide
head(bp)
getwd()
system("git rev-parse --show-toplevel")
file.exists(".git")
list.files("butterflies_pesticides.xlsx", all.files = TRUE)
bp
```
## Q1. Normality test 

```{r}
#Independent t-test
shapiro.test(bp$`Wing Length`)
```

## Q.2 Equality of variances test

```{r}
head(bp)
var.test(`Wing Length`~ Group, data=bp)
```
## Q.3 Statistical test

```{r}
#Welch's t-test
t.test(`Wing Length`~ Group, data=bp,
            alternative=c("two.sided"),
            var.equal=FALSE,
            )
```

## Q.ggplot 

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(bp, aes(x=Group, y=`Wing Length`))+
  geom_boxplot()
```
## Q.5 

```{r}
#I wanted to research whether there were significant differences in wing length between two groups of butterflies: one group that was exposed to pesticides during the larval stage and another group that received no treatment (control). Using an independent Welch’s t-test, I ran the code and compared the wing length measurements of 80 butterflies, 40 from each of the two groups. The results showed a significant difference in wing length between the two groups (t = 3.982, df = 66.029, p-value = 0.0001721). These results suggests that pesticide exposure during larval development may have an effect on butterfly wing length, resulting in differences between treated and untreated individuals.
```
